questions.question: What should the rate limiter use to identify clients? Options: client IP address, authenticated user ID, API key, or a combination?
questions.rationale: This is a requirements gap that affects security posture and user-facing behavior. Cannot be deferred to architects because it changes what the system does, not how it's built.

deferredToArchitecture.rationale: Algorithm choice (token bucket vs sliding window) is a design decision; all options satisfy the stated requirements
Whether config is declarative, decorator-based, or inline is a code organization decision for architects to evaluate against codebase patterns
Redis is already specified; atomic operation strategy (MULTI/EXEC vs Lua scripts) is implementation detail
Fail-open vs fail-closed is a design trade-off architects can evaluate
X-RateLimit-Limit/Remaining/Reset are standard practice; architects can decide inclusion

acceptanceCriteria: Middleware can be applied per-route with configurable rate limits
Health endpoints can be configured as unlimited (bypass)
Auth endpoints rate limited to 5 requests/minute
General API endpoints rate limited to 100 requests/minute
Uses Redis via existing src/config/redis.ts connection for token bucket state
Returns HTTP 429 with Retry-After header when rate exceeded
Integrates into existing middleware chain in src/middleware/ without breaking auth flow

gateStatus.blockedOn: User response to rate limit key strategy question (Q1)
